question: 1. How many players are on a GAA Gaelic football or hurling team on the pitch at the start of a match?
explanation: Standard GAA teams field 15 players per side at the start of competitive matches.

question: 2. What is the name of the famous GAA stadium in Dublin?
explanation: Croke Park in north Dublin is the headquarters and primary stadium of the Gaelic Athletic Association.

question: 3. In which sport is the Wimbledon Championships played?
explanation: Wimbledon is the world's oldest tennis tournament, contested on outdoor grass courts.

question: 4. What is the name of the small, hard ball used in hurling and camogie?
explanation: The sliotar has a cork core covered in stitched leather with raised ribs.

question: 5. How many points is a goal worth in Gaelic football and hurling?
explanation: A goal scored into the net is worth three points, equivalent to three points scored over the crossbar.

question: 6. In which sport would you use a driver, iron, and putter?
explanation: Golfers use woods/drivers for distance, irons for approach shots, and putters on the green.

question: 7. How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
explanation: The modern Olympic Games are scheduled in an Olympiad cycle of every four years.

question: 8. What colour card does a soccer referee show to send a player off the pitch?
explanation: A red card signifies direct dismissal or accumulation of two yellow card offences.

question: 9. In which sport do players score a "slam dunk"?
explanation: A slam dunk occurs when a basketball player jumps and forcibly thrusts the ball through the hoop.

question: 10. What is the name of the trophy awarded to the winners of the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship?
explanation: The Sam Maguire Cup has been presented to the All-Ireland Senior Football champions since 1928.

question: 11. What is the name of the trophy awarded to the winners of the All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship?
explanation: The Liam MacCarthy Cup is awarded annually to the All-Ireland Senior Hurling champions.

question: 12. In boxing, how many rounds are in a standard men's world title fight?
explanation: Championship professional boxing bouts are contested over a maximum of 12 rounds of three minutes each.

question: 13. Which Irish boxer won Olympic gold in London 2012 and became an undisputed world champion?
explanation: Katie Taylor won gold at London 2012 and unified world lightweight titles as a professional.

question: 14. In rugby union, how many players are on each team on the pitch?
explanation: Rugby union teams feature 15 active players (8 forwards and 7 backs) per side on the field.

question: 15. What is the name of the stadium in Dublin where Ireland plays its home international rugby and soccer matches?
explanation: The Aviva Stadium at Lansdowne Road is Ireland's home ground for international rugby union and association football.

question: 16. In snooker, what colour ball is worth the most points (7 points)?
explanation: The black ball is worth 7 points, followed by pink (6), blue (5), brown (4), green (3), yellow (2), and red (1).

question: 17. In athletics, how many metres are in a standard outdoor running track lap?
explanation: Lane 1 of a standard regulation outdoor athletics track measures exactly 400 metres.

question: 18. Which county won the 2026 All-Ireland Senior Camogie Championship, defeating Galway in the final?
explanation: Cork defeated Galway to capture the 2026 Senior Camogie title.

question: 19. Which French club won the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League, beating Arsenal on penalties in the final?
explanation: Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) clinched the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League crown in a penalty shootout.

question: 20. Who won the 2026 Wimbledon Men's Singles title, defeating Alexander Zverev in the final?
explanation: Jannik Sinner defeated Alexander Zverev on Centre Court to win Wimbledon 2026.

question: 21. Who won the 2026 Tour de France, claiming his fifth overall title?
explanation: Tadej Pogačar sealed his 5th Tour de France general classification triumph in July 2026.

question: 22. In tennis, what word is used for a score of zero?
explanation: In tennis scoring, 'love' indicates zero (derived from the French 'l'oeuf' meaning egg).

question: 23. How many points is a try worth in rugby union?
explanation: Grounding the ball in the in-goal area earns 5 points for a try.

question: 24. In golf, what term is used for completing a hole in one stroke under par?
explanation: A score of 1-under par on an individual hole is called a birdie.

question: 25. Which Irish swimmer won gold in the 800m freestyle at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
explanation: Daniel Wiffen from County Armagh won gold in Olympic record time in the men's 800m freestyle in Paris.

question: 26. Which Irish gymnast won gold on the pommel horse at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
explanation: Rhys McClenaghan of County Down secured Ireland's first ever Olympic gymnastics gold medal.

question: 27. In which sport is the Stanley Cup awarded?
explanation: The Stanley Cup is the championship trophy awarded to the NHL playoff winners in professional ice hockey.

question: 28. How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in tennis each year?
explanation: The four major Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon, and US Open.

question: 29. In cricket, how many players are on a team?
explanation: A standard cricket team fields 11 players.

question: 30. Which country has won the FIFA Men's World Cup the most times (5 times)?
explanation: Brazil has won five World Cup tournaments (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).

question: 31. What is the distance of a marathon to the nearest kilometre?
explanation: The official marathon distance is 42.195 kilometres (26 miles 385 yards).

question: 32. In Formula 1 racing, what colour flag is waved to signal the end of a race?
explanation: The black-and-white chequered flag signals the completion of the Grand Prix.

question: 33. Which Northern Irish golfer has won four major championships, including the US Open and The Open?
explanation: Rory McIlroy from Holywood, County Down, has won four major championship titles.

question: 34. In Gaelic games, what is the name of the trophy awarded to the winners of the All-Ireland Senior Camogie Championship?
explanation: The O'Duffy Cup is presented to the victorious All-Ireland Senior Camogie team.

question: 35. Who won the 2026 Wimbledon Women's Singles title, defeating Karolína Muchová in an all-Czech final?
explanation: Linda Nosková captured her maiden Grand Slam singles title at Wimbledon 2026.

question: 36. In which European city was the 2026 UEFA Champions League Final played?
explanation: The 2026 UEFA Champions League Final was staged at the Puskás Aréna in Budapest, Hungary.

question: 37. Beginning with V, what is the name of the wooden stadium cycling track used in Olympic track cycling?
explanation: A velodrome features steeply banked oval tracks purpose-built for track cycling.

question: 38. In rowing, what is the name of the person who sits at the stern and steers the boat without rowing?
explanation: The coxswain (or cox) steers the shell, calls cadence, and executes race strategy.

question: 39. Beginning with E, what is the name of the golf score that is two strokes under par on a single hole?
explanation: An eagle represents scoring 2 strokes under par on a given hole.

question: 40. Which Irish county has won the most All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships?
explanation: Kilkenny leads the all-time roll of honour with 36 Senior Hurling titles.

question: 41. Which Irish county has won the most All-Ireland Senior Football Championships?
explanation: Kerry tops the all-time leaderboard with 38 All-Ireland Senior Football crowns.

question: 42. In fencing, what are the three types of swords used?
explanation: Olympic fencing competitions are held using foil, épée, and sabre weapons.

question: 43. Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
explanation: The inaugural 1896 modern Olympic Games took place at the Panathenaic Stadium in Athens.

question: 44. In badminton, what is the feathered projectile hit over the net called?
explanation: A shuttlecock (or birdie) is made of 16 natural feathers embedded into a rounded cork base.

question: 45. Beginning with B, what is the name of the Winter Olympic sport that combines cross-country skiing and rifle shooting?
explanation: Biathlon tests cross-country skate-ski endurance paired with precision small-bore rifle marksmanship.

question: 46. In darts, what is the highest possible score you can achieve with a single dart?
explanation: Hitting the inner narrow treble ring of the 20 segment scores 3 × 20 = 60 points.

question: 47. Which country won the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France?
explanation: The Springboks of South Africa edged New Zealand 12–11 at the Stade de France to defend their crown.

question: 48. In athletics, what is the name of the 10-event men's competition?
explanation: The decathlon comprises 10 track and field events contested over two consecutive days.

question: 49. Which Irish sprinter broke multiple national records and reached the 400m final at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
explanation: Rhasidat Adeleke set Irish national sprint records and placed 4th in the Olympic 400m final in Paris.

question: 50. In horse racing, what is the name of the famous steeplechase held every April at Aintree near Liverpool?
explanation: The Grand National is a handicap steeplechase run over 4 miles 2½ furlongs with 30 fences.
